text: Not necessarily. It depends on the game and on how much time people spend on it. Strategy and puzzle games can improve problem-solving and concentration, and some online games involve a lot of teamwork. But if someone plays for six hours a day instead of studying or sleeping, then obviously it's become a problem. So I'd say games aren't the issue — excessive playing is.

tips.en: It depends on the game and on how much time says exactly what it depends on.
tips.kk: It depends on the game and on how much time — нақты неге байланысты екенін атайсыз.
tips.ru: It depends on the game and on how much time — называете, от чего именно зависит.
tips.example: It depends on the game and on how much time people spend on it

tips.en: Games aren't the issue, excessive playing is: a short, precise formula.
tips.kk: Games aren't the issue — excessive playing is — қысқа әрі дәл формула.
tips.ru: Games aren't the issue — excessive playing is — короткая и точная формула.

text: I can see both sides. Professional gamers train for hours every day, need lightning-fast reactions and compete in huge tournaments with prize money, so in some ways it is a sport. On the other hand, most people associate sport with physical effort, and sitting at a computer doesn't really fit that idea. Personally, I'd call it a competition of skill rather than a sport.

tips.en: I can see both sides signals arguments for and against.
tips.kk: I can see both sides — әрі қарай қолдайтын және қарсы дәлелдер болатынын білдіреді.
tips.ru: I can see both sides — сигнал, что дальше будут доводы за и против.

tips.en: A competition of skill rather than a sport offers a precise definition.
tips.kk: A competition of skill rather than a sport — дәл анықтама ұсынасыз.
tips.ru: A competition of skill rather than a sport — вы предлагаете точное определение.

text: Absolutely. Games turn practice into something people actually want to do. Language apps, for example, use points and levels to keep learners coming back every day, and history games can make students curious about a period they'd otherwise find boring. Of course, games can't replace a teacher, but as a tool for repetition and motivation, they work remarkably well.

tips.en: Games turn practice into something people actually want to do is the core of the answer.
tips.kk: Games turn practice into something people actually want to do — жауаптың өзегі.
tips.ru: Games turn practice into something people actually want to do — суть ответа.

text: I think some limits are reasonable, especially on school nights, because gaming can easily eat into sleep and homework. But the way parents do it matters. If they simply ban games, teenagers usually find a way around the rules. It works much better when the family agrees on limits together and the parents explain why, so teenagers learn to control their own time.

tips.en: Especially on school nights makes the position specific.
tips.kk: Especially on school nights — нақтылау ұстанымды нақты етеді.
tips.ru: Especially on school nights — уточнение делает позицию конкретной.

text: Mainly because they fit into short gaps in the day. People can play for five minutes on the bus or while waiting in a queue, and most mobile games are free to download. They're also designed to be addictive, with daily rewards that make you want to come back. I suspect that's why so many adults play them without calling themselves gamers.

tips.en: They fit into short gaps in the day, followed by the bus and the queue as examples.
